data.narrative:
Red 6, a Series B+ defense and security company that has raised $100M+, operates within a sector containing 23 identifiable peers across public and private markets. The comp universe includes two public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and eight private firms, with top-tier private peers including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable to this analysis. Despite identifying 23 same-sector peers, filtering by stage, proximity, and valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints in any narrow cohort. Zero same-stage comparables, zero adjacent-stage comparables, and zero similar-tier private companies satisfied the minimum threshold of three observations required for reliable peer-median triangulation. Recourse to all-sector median metrics would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of defense and security subsectors.

Without sufficient narrow peer density to support quantitative triangulation, valuation determination requires reliance on alternative methods not detailed in the provided dataset. The analytical constraint here reflects a structural limitation of the frontier-defense market: rapid technical differentiation and stage-specific dynamics create sparse comparable sets. Any valuation range derived from this exercise should be qualified by acknowledgment of sparse comparable support and elevated uncertainty around fair-value placement relative to the identified peer universe.
